title: Fixed by AI, Flagged as AI: A Matched Audit of AI-Text Detectors on 12,132 Student Essays
description:
A 2023 Stanford study reported that AI-text detectors flag most essays by non-native English writers as AI-generated, comparing 91 TOEFL answers with essays by US students on other topics. This project repeats the test with a matched design: 12,132 student essays, including 8,244 in which English learners and native speakers in US schools answered the same prompts (PERSUADE 2.0, ELLIPSE), 2,989 AI-written essays on those prompts, and nine open detectors released between 2019 and 2025.

On the original TOEFL essays the result holds (43–97% flagged by trained detectors). On matched essays it does not: 7 of 9 detectors flag English learners significantly less often than native speakers, and none flags them more often. A light grammar correction by a language model raises false flags for every detector (up to 57 times for English learners' essays), while a dictionary spellcheck barely changes them. The archive contains the paper, code, per-essay detector scores and the results website.
